interest: This document is of significant interest as an intelligence artifact created on the eve of the Pacific War. Dated mid-November 1941—barely three weeks prior to the attack on Pearl Harbor—it captures the U.S. State Department and military intelligence tracking rumors and reports of Japanese forward military expansion, specifically the construction of air and naval bases in the Paracel Islands in the South China Sea.
overview: This file consists of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form 1932) for the U.S. State Department decimal file 894.245 ('Equipment And Supplies., Japan, Military Bases'). The sheet catalogs incoming reports from November 1941 concerning Japanese military installations, specifically noting two entries derived from Military Attaché (Japan) Report No. 351 dated November 15, 1941. These entries record intelligence and rumors regarding Japan's establishment of naval and air bases in the Paracel Islands shortly before the outbreak of the Pacific War.

subfiles.about: A State Department docket sheet indexing intelligence reports regarding Japanese naval and air bases in the Paracel Islands.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet records documents filed under decimal classification 894.245 regarding Japanese military bases. It indexes report No. 351 from the U.S. Military Attaché in Japan, dated November 15, 1941, reporting rumors that Japan was establishing naval and air bases in the Paracel Islands. A related cross-reference note directs attention to decimal file 894.345 and sub-number 894.245/1.
